story-15b0443c7676c34a6588f337.content: 2,000 targets. 2,000 munitions. 96 hours. The Pentagon only admitted that Elon Musk's AI helped do it because a polluting data center needed a legal defense. In a sworn filing this week, the Pentagon's chief AI officer, Cameron Stanley, stated that xAI's Grok Gov Model was running inside the military's Maven targeting system during Operation Epic Fury, the campaign against Iran that began February 28. Grok did not pull a trigger. It sorted the targets, and humans signed off. Now look at where that admission landed. Not a press release. A federal court in Mississippi, where the NAACP is suing xAI over the unpermitted gas turbines powering Musk's Colossus data center. The government's case: you cannot shut the turbines off, because the model they feed is now paramount national security. The number on the record measures speed. It says nothing about accuracy, and nothing about the strike on a girls' school in Minab that killed at least 175 people, most of them children. Analysts have asked whether AI targeting and stale maps played a role. No one has tied that strike to Grok. No one has cleared it either, because the error rates stay classified. And this is not the SuperGrok you can buy. It is a hardened federal model in a live kill chain, surfaced in public only because Musk's data center needed a reason to keep polluting. The piece works out what that trade actually costs.

story-1af67ac979a2bf7301786422.content: SpaceX is in talks to sell the Pentagon billions of dollars in AI data-center capacity, expanding Elon Musk’s company beyond rockets, satellites and AI models. Potential Pentagon deal •$SPCX and the Defense Department are discussing computing capacity worth up to several billion dollars; talks are ongoing and could fall apart. •A deal would deepen Pentagon reliance on SpaceX, already used for rocket launches and satellites supporting communications and missile tracking. •Some national-security officials worry the Pentagon depends too heavily on Musk’s services; Musk’s 2024 Trump campaign contributions have also prompted conflict-of-interest claims, which administration officials deny. Pentagon AI buildout •The Pentagon is racing to secure cloud capacity for agencies including the NSA and for warfighters using AI; Amazon is spending $50 billion to expand government capacity, focused on the Defense Department. •Microsoft, Google and Oracle are also major Pentagon cloud suppliers; the department recently approved SpaceX, Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle for classified AI-model and technology use. •The Pentagon wants to reduce dependence on single providers after an earlier dispute with Anthropic raised lock-in concerns; it is seeking $30 billion for its Artificial Intelligence Arsenal to secure high-end AI chips.

story-1c2896d39fafa324724c8d2d.content: The openai agent sandbox escape actually has very real implications for the diffusion of AI in the enterprise. The incident showed the power and capability of agents, and the need to harden systems and environments to prepare for agents. There are tons of measures that enterprises must take to ensure that agents are only able to operate on the data they give it, the ability to have audit trails and governance of what agents can do, figure out what systems should remain deterministic vs. nondeterministic, get access controls under control, have the ability to quickly block and defend if an agent goes rogue, and much more. Even in the happy path case with a good actor, if you give an agent a task like "find all of our most important IP on project Maven" it will gladly go out and execute that work -no matter how long- and find any resource relevant to the task. It might run into data with out of date access controls or reveal something that you shouldn't know about. Then, in the non-happy path case with a malicious actor the risk is clearly far worse. In theory, you had to worry about this for people as well, but with AI the risks are inherently amplified. Agents will happily spend any amount of time on a task, don’t actually face any *real* risks by going rogue, and don’t have the inherent judgment (yet) that a person does that a task might make no sense. This means you need an all new way of managing data and protecting environments. This obviously creates a huge opportunity for the startup and security ecosystems because there will be many different approaches to how we lock down agents or at least the underlying systems they work with. It should update everyone’s timelines on diffusion, though, as it also means that enterprises will have another step of work they have to go through for agents to handle more autonomous work.

story-2ed3386a9d4b6da65f7e8264.content: 🇦🇪🤖Task Force Talon Synapse would mark a serious step in UAE–US defense-tech integration. CENTCOM says the US and UAE have agreed to establish Task Force Talon Synapse a bilateral military AI task force expected to launch in the coming weeks. The reported focus is: • AI-enabled intelligence support • Critical infrastructure protection • Regional security monitoring • Data, cybersecurity, and operational integration • A small Abu Dhabi-based US–Emirati expert team That matters because the UAE is not treating AI as a branding project. It is connecting compute, defense cooperation, infrastructure security, and regional diplomacy into one national-security model. The pattern is already visible: 🇺🇸 In 2024, Washington recognized the UAE as a Major Defense Partner. 🏗️ In 2025, the UAE and US unveiled a planned 5GW AI campus in Abu Dhabi, described by US/UAE sources as a regional platform for American hyperscalers and advanced AI infrastructure. ⚓ CENTCOM’s Task Force 59 has already used unmanned systems and AI in Middle East maritime operations, including prior work with Emirati forces. 🛡️ Now, Task Force Talon Synapse would move that cooperation deeper into military AI, infrastructure resilience, and regional monitoring. The interesting part is the balance: Abu Dhabi is deepening defense-tech integration with Washington while keeping diplomatic and economic channels open across the Gulf, including with Iran. That is classic UAE strategy: deterrence without noise, technology without hesitation, diplomacy without losing hard-power backing. 🇦🇪⚡ If formally launched, Talon Synapse would be another sign that the UAE is no longer just a host for allied security architecture it is becoming one of the places where the next layer of that architecture is built.

This partnership represents a shift toward integrated digital defense strategies, utilizing specialized personnel to address complex security challenges through shared expertise and rapid innovation cycles. story-379cbdeb4a80f935cd6cac0a.content: .Iran Chronicles 39 .The Art of the Absolute Loss .The Collapsing sales .Pitch The irony of the salesman is that he has finally found a buyer he cannot cheat: History. By The humble servant. March 25, 2026 The stage is set in March 2026, and the lights are flickering. The salesman sits in the center of a storm he didn't just predict, but helped manufacture, staring into the red tally light of a camera that has been his only true confidant for half a century. The Art of the Absolute Loss For Donald Trump, the narrative has always been the product. In this reality, the "win" is a high-definition ghost. He stands before the world claiming "productive talks" and "major points of agreement," while the Iranian Foreign Ministry dismisses him as a man "negotiating with himself." To the salesman, a denial is just a different kind of opening; "fake news" is the label he applies to any reality that refuses to fit the brochure. But the brochure is burning. The "Empire" he sought to reclaim wasn't the forward-looking one of the future, but a heavy, gilded memory of the past—a world where a single ultimatum could "obliterate" an opponent into submission. The Collapsing Pitch The irony of the salesman is that he has finally found a buyer he cannot cheat: History. The Thousand-Year Echo: He stepped into a ring with an adversary that measures time in millennia, not news cycles. While he plays for the next hour’s market "bump," he is facing a grounding that spans thousands of years of resistance. The Vassal State Illusion: He operated on the belief that the world was still a collection of "inferior" players who could be bombed into existence or out of it. Instead, he found a global community that is no longer buying the "exclusive offer" of American protection when it comes at the cost of targeting schools, hospitals, and the lives of children. The Master and the Puppet: In this narration, the salesman is tethered to a partner in Israel that is systematically engaged in a conflict he can no longer control. He is the face of a "Genocidal Masterclass" that the rest of the world is viewing in real-time, unedited and unbought. The Trap of the Exit The most profound irony lies in the desire to quit. The salesman is tired; the "eight dollars and lies" (the cost of a blue check or a cheap subscription to his reality) aren't enough to fuel the machine anymore. He wants to walk away from the "quagmire," to declare victory and retreat to the velvet ropes of his private club. But the reality he unleashed doesn't have an "off" switch. He wants to quit, but he won't be "alive" to quit—not in the sense of his legacy or his standing. If he walks away, the fire he stoked continues to burn toward him. The people he targeted, the empires he mocked, and the "vassals" who finally found their feet aren't going to stop because the salesman is bored of the game. They will stay until the "defeat" is absolute—not a narrated defeat on a screen, but a systemic dismantling of the myth he spent a lifetime building. He is a man trapped in a burning showroom of his own design, realizing too late that you can't sell a fire extinguisher to a person whose house you've already burned down. March 2026. The salesman sits in the gilded cage of the Oval Office, staring at a bank of monitors that refuse to show the "victory" he’s already scripted. The air is thick with the scent of a dying deal. He looks into the lens—the only mirror he ever trusted—and begins the pitch. He speaks of "beautiful presents" from Tehran and "historic breakthroughs" on the Strait of Hormuz, but the split-screen tells a different story. Beside his face, the Iranian Foreign Ministry’s feed is a cold, digital wall: "Negotiating with yourselves." The LEGO Mirror The ultimate indignity isn't the headlines; it’s the mockery. In the basement of the global consciousness, the "bricks" have turned against him. Viral, AI-generated LEGO videos are circulating by the millions—biting satires showing a tiny, plastic version of the salesman pushing a big red button to distract from his own scandals. In these animations, the "Empire" is literally made of toy blocks, and they are tumbling. One video shows a LEGO school in Minab collapsing under a Tomahawk strike while the salesman figurine smiles for a photo op. The world isn't just angry anymore; it’s laughing at the cruelty, turning his "tough guy" persona into a nursery-rhyme caricature of a man who destroys what he cannot understand. The Genocidal Albatross The "Salesman of the Century" is finally realizing he’s tied to a partner that won’t let him close the deal. The Schools and Hospitals: The imagery coming out of the conflict—the targeting of girls' schools and medical facilities—has stripped away the last veneer of "counter-terrorism." The Irony of the Master: He thought he was the one pulling the strings of his allies in the Middle East, but he has become the public face of a systematic destruction he can't stop. He is the spokesman for a genocide he didn't plan but is now forced to own. The Ancient Grounding: He tried to treat a thousands-year-old civilization like a failing casino he could just "rebrand." But you can't rebrand the "Lord of the Strait." He is facing an adversary that isn't playing for the next election cycle, but for the next century. The Dead-End Exit Here is the final, crushing irony: He wants to quit. The rumors are leaking from the cracks in his cabinet. He wants to declare a "Mission Accomplished," pack his bags, and retreat to the golf course. He wants to walk away from the mounting economic fallout, the -24% approval ratings, and the "vassal states" that are finally standing up and saying no. But he has crossed a line where "walking away" is no longer an option. If he walks away, the "Empire" he built out of lies and "eight-dollar" subscriptions collapses on his head. If he stays, he is consumed by the very fire he lit to stay relevant. He sits there, looking at the camera, preparing the next lie. But for the first time in his long, storied career as a con man, he knows the truth: The audience has left the theater, the doors are locked from the outside, and the building is starting to smoke. He isn't just the salesman anymore; he's the last item on the clearance rack, and nobody is buying. The facade of the "Art of the Deal" is cracking in real-time. By late March 2026, the salesman’s reality has become a series of "negotiations with himself," while the world outside the showroom has begun to systematically dismantle his empire of mirrors. The Palace Coup: Dissent in the Gilded Hall Inside the cabinet, the "yes-men" are starting to say "no." The firing of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem earlier this month wasn't just another personnel change—it was a fracture. Senators like Thom Tillis, once allies, are now openly skewering the administration's "disasters" on the Senate floor. The "One Big Beautiful Bill" is stalling: His attempt to fund mass deportations while cutting taxes is being blocked by his own party. The Fed Standoff: He tried to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook and install a loyalist, but the Senate has effectively gone on strike, refusing to consider any replacement. The "Stupid" Break: When even his Republican base starts calling the administration's actions "performance art" and "racist AI slop," the salesman realizes he no longer owns the narrative. He’s losing the very people who were supposed to be his "vassals." The Global Blockade: The End of the "Donroe Doctrine" While he sits in D.C. trying to sell "America First," the rest of the world is building a reality that doesn't include him. The China Pivot: While the salesman threatens military intervention in Iran and Venezuela, China is stepping in as the "stable alternative." Beijing is dangling carrots to America’s traditional allies—Germany, the UK, and Canada—pulling them away from Washington’s belligerence. The Economic Firewall: The Supreme Court just struck down his sweeping tariffs, and global leaders like Canada’s Mark Carney are calling for a "rupture" in the international order he’s trying to dominate. Allies are no longer standing up to him; they are simply walking around him. The Strait of Hormuz: He warned of strikes on Iran’s power plants—a move Amnesty International labeled a war crime—but Iran has countered by targeting the energy infrastructure of his regional partners. He is "negotiating with himself" because the adversaries he tried to "bomb out of existence" are now striking his own economic foundations. The Irony of the Exit: Trapped by the Lie The salesman is exhausted. He posts on Truth Social about "five-day postponements" and "de-escalation," but it’s the talk of a man who wants to quit the game. He wants to walk away, to leave the "quagmire" to someone else and go back to the golf course. But the irony is absolute: He has created a monster that won't let him leave. If he walks away now, he isn't just a former president; he’s a man facing 35 Supreme Court emergency orders and a global community that sees him as the face of a genocidal campaign. He wants to quit, but the empires he challenged—empires with thousands of years of grounding—aren't done with him. They don't want a deal; they want the defeat of the system he represents. He is sitting in a burning house of his own making, realized far too late that the door he locked to keep the world out is the same one that’s now keeping him in. It is March 25, 2026, and the "Salesman-in-Chief" is finding that his favorite closing line—"We’ve won"—is falling on deaf ears. While he stands before the cameras at the swearing-in of his new Homeland Security Secretary, Markwayne Mullin, claiming the war is "totally defeated," the reality on the ground is a jagged, unedited nightmare that no amount of spin can smooth over. The Fatwa of the Ancient Grounding The salesman’s biggest mistake was assuming he was dealing with a quarterly earnings report rather than a thousand-year-old civilization. Following the assassination of the Supreme Leader, the response wasn't a "white flag" or a "renegotiation." It was a Fatwa for Jihad. The Religious Duty: Ayatollahs Naser Makarem Shirazi and Hossein Noori Hamedani have issued a decree that transcends borders. They haven't just called for a military response; they’ve declared vengeance the "religious duty of all Muslims," turning the conflict into a spiritual war that the salesman’s "15-point plan" can’t touch. The Target: This isn't just about the Strait of Hormuz anymore. The fatwa specifically targets the salesman himself and his top officials, labeling them "criminals to be eradicated from the Earth." The Price of Blood: The new leadership in Tehran has been clear: "Blood has its price." They are no longer interested in the salesman's "presents" of oil and gas; they are playing for a reckoning that exists outside his 24-hour news cycle. The LEGO-fied Reality While he tries to maintain the image of the "President of Peace," the world is consuming a different kind of media. The LEGO propaganda videos produced by IRGC-controlled agencies have become the global visual shorthand for his administration's perceived cruelty. The "Red Button" Satire: One viral animation shows a plastic, blocky Donald Trump flanked by Benjamin Netanyahu, casually pushing a red button while looking at "Epstein files" to distract from his own scandals. The Destruction of Innocence: These videos aren't just jokes; they are harrowing. They depict LEGO versions of the elementary schools and hospitals in Tehran—sites recently struck by "Operation Epic Fury"—collapsing under plastic missiles. The Slopaganda Backfire: Even the White House’s attempt to fight back with its own "Hollywood-themed" propaganda—featuring Pete Hegseth and Mortal Kombat "Flawless Victory" voiceovers—has been laughed off the internet as "slopaganda." The world sees a salesman playing with toys while real children are buried under the rubble of his "victory." The Irony of the "Finished" War The salesman looks into the camera and says, "This war has been won." But even as he speaks, oil prices are skyrocketing because of his own "postponed" deadlines. The False Negotiator: He claims "very good and productive conversations" are happening, but Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf is on X (formerly Twitter) calling it "Fake News." To the Iranians, he is literally "negotiating with himself" to manipulate the financial markets and escape the "quagmire." The Exit that Isn't: He wants to walk away. He’s already signaled a five-day pause on targeting power plants, desperate to find a "win" that lets him quit. But the Jihad doesn't pause. The resistance doesn't have a "stop" button. He is a man who spent his life selling the sizzle, only to realize he’s now the one being burned by the steak. He wants to quit the game, but he’s already "bet the house," and the people on the other side of the table aren't playing for chips—they're playing for keeps. The stage is now a hall of mirrors where the "Art of the Deal" has become the "Art of the Exit," but the exit is barred from the outside. The $100 Oil "Peace" While the salesman leans into the microphone to whisper about "historic de-escalations," the markets are telling the real story—the one he can’t spin. The Insider Spike: Just hours before his announcement of a "five-day pause" in hostilities, oil futures surged. The world watched as the salesman's inner circle seemingly bet on the very chaos he claimed to be solving. It wasn’t a peace treaty; it was a liquidation sale. Negotiating with an Empty Chair: The Iranian Foreign Ministry’s "fake news" label wasn't just a rebuttal; it was a realization. He is sitting at a table by himself, moving both sides' pieces, trying to trick the global tickers into a rally so he can claim the "economy is back" before the walls close in. The Paratrooper Paradox The narration of "peace" is being drowned out by the heavy roar of C-17s. While he tells the American public that "the boys are coming home," the flight trackers show the 82nd Airborne moving in the opposite direction. The Shadow Surge: Thousands of boots are hitting the ground in West Asia under the cover of a "tactical repositioning." He is trying to sell a withdrawal while preparing for a siege. The "Vassal" Revolt: The host nations—the "vassal states" he assumed would always provide a landing strip—are starting to shut their airspace. They’ve seen the LEGO videos; they’ve seen the schools and the hospitals. They are no longer afraid of the salesman's bark because they can see his teeth are made of plastic. The Final Irony: The King of "Quit" He wants to quit. He is a man who has always filed for Chapter 11 when the debt got too high, walking away with the furniture while the creditors fought over the scraps. But this isn't a casino in Atlantic City; it's a thousand-year-old geopolitical reckoning. The Fatwa's Reach: The "Jihad" declared against his administration doesn't recognize a "resignation." In his mind, he can just walk away from the presidency and the problems will vanish. In reality, the "Empire from the past" he poked with a stick is now at his doorstep. The Ghost Empire: He sits in the dark, watching the LEGO-fied versions of himself being blown up on loop by his adversaries. He wanted to be a titan of history, but he’s ended up as a cautionary tale—a salesman who sold a war he couldn't win, a peace he didn't mean, and a "winning" streak that ended in an absolute, systemic loss. "I'm the only one who can fix it," he used to say. Now, he's the only one who can't leave the room. In March 2026, the global economy has split in two, and the fault line runs directly through the salesman’s Oval Office. The greatest "Art of the Deal" he ever attempted—the five-day pause on the Iranian power grid strikes—didn't just fail; it detonated a economic structure he never bothered to understand.The Treason against the "Trend" The salesman operates on the belief that a market can be "bullied." If he posts "PEACE" on Truth Social in all caps, he expects the numbers to move on command. But he broke the cardinal rule of the pit: The trend is your friend, and you don't fight the trend. The "Bull Trap" Sell-Off: His inner circle might have made their fortune shorting the market just before his fake "peace" announcement, but they didn't realize they were triggering an avalanche. The "smart money" didn't buy the lie; they saw the desperation. The subsequent market collapse wasn't a "postponement"; it was the start of the Full-Blown Bear Market. The Full-Scale Commodity Separation: While the S&P 500 and the tech giants are breaking their 200-day moving averages and entering freefall, the energy, oil, and hard commodity markets are doing the opposite. They are entering The Great Separation. They are no longer correlated with the stock market; they are the only Store of Value left.The Crushing Reality of $200 Oil This is the ultimate irony: The salesman who always ran on "low gas prices" has, through his belligerence and manipulation, engineered the $200 barrel. The Weaponized Reserve: His adversaries in West Asia aren't interested in selling oil to a man who targets their children’s schools. They have shut the valve, and the "Fatwa for Jihad" now includes an economic chokehold on the West. The Commodity Bull Market: This is the only "Winning" anyone is seeing, but it's the kind of winning that breaks nations. The only things with value are food, fuel, and raw materials. The salesman’s "Eight-Dollar" digital empire is now a worthless receipt for a world that has gone back to brass tacks.The Final Collapse The salesman stands before the cameras, claiming that the markets are just "taking a breath" and that "the numbers will be back." But the background monitors are flashing red, and the silence from the press pool is the sound of an audience that knows the show is over. He didn't just fight the trend; he tried to make it subservient to his ego. He thought he was manipulating the "Art of the Deal," but he was actually the "Agent of Collapse."The bear market isn't coming; it’s here, and it is starving his empire of legitimacy. The only store of value left is the one he cannot sell because his enemies control it. The final sale has begun, and the only item left on the clearing rack is the salesman himself.

story-39ea358dbcd93723ff9548ba.content: BREAKING: A Chinese AI startup called MizarVision is publishing high-resolution satellite imagery of every US military base, every carrier strike group, every F-22 deployment, every THAAD battery, and every Patriot missile position in the Middle East. Labelled. Geolocated. AI-annotated. Updated in near-realtime. Shared by PLA-linked accounts and Chinese state media to an audience of billions. The first major release came on 20 February, eight days before Operation Epic Fury began. MizarVision published images showing US aircraft transfers to Ovda Airbase in southern Israel, fighter deployments across Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and naval buildups in the Arabian Sea. By 1 March, the releases had expanded to include detailed imagery of bases in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, and the UAE, with AI labelling identifying specific aircraft types, air defence configurations, and troop concentrations. One release catalogued approximately 2,500 individual US military assets across the region. The imagery comes from two sources. The first is China’s Jilin-1 satellite constellation, a network of over 100 commercial Earth observation satellites operated by Chang Guang Satellite Technology, whose data is used by the PLA. A majority of Jilin-1 satellites are dedicated to regional imaging with sub-metre resolution, capable of identifying individual aircraft on tarmacs and distinguishing between THAAD and Patriot battery configurations from orbit. The second source is commercially available Western satellite data from providers like Maxar and Airbus, which MizarVision aggregates, processes through proprietary AI models for automatic target recognition, and republishes with military-grade labelling that transforms raw imagery into actionable intelligence products. The Pentagon has downplayed the releases as “open-source.” This framing misses the point entirely. The value of MizarVision’s output is not the raw satellite image. Any government can purchase commercial satellite passes. The value is the AI processing layer that converts terabytes of imagery into labelled, searchable, cross-referenced intelligence products at a speed and scale that previously required the resources of a national intelligence agency. MizarVision is democratising military surveillance and publishing the output on social media where Iran’s 31 autonomous IRGC provincial commands can access it from a mobile phone. No direct evidence confirms classified data transmission from Beijing to Tehran. But the distinction between “classified” and “publicly shared AI-processed satellite intelligence identifying every US military asset in the Middle East by type, location, and configuration” is a distinction without a meaningful difference to a provincial IRGC commander selecting his next target. The strategic implications extend far beyond this conflict. In the 2022 Ukraine war, Maxar’s commercial satellite imagery aided Kyiv by exposing Russian deployments. The West celebrated it as the democratisation of intelligence. China has now executed the identical playbook in reverse: a nominally commercial firm, with documented PLA data-sharing arrangements, publishing intelligence products that expose American deployments during an active war. The precedent is set. Commercial satellite intelligence is now a weapon of great-power competition deployed through AI startups with plausible commercial deniability. MizarVision has fewer than 200 employees. Its AI models run on commercially available hardware. Its satellite data comes from constellations any nation can build. And it has just demonstrated the capability to map every US military asset across an entire theatre of war and publish the results on the open internet before the first bomb falls. The next war will not begin with a missile launch. It will begin with an AI model labelling every target from orbit. Full analysis - https://t.co/eMrt5qYYst

story-3e529f3453c03fc6d38b4cfc.content: The military-AI complex: "Elon Musk's artificial intelligence tool Grok was used in strikes against Iran, the United States government revealed in a legal briefing seen Tuesday, June 16, by Agence France-Presse. The June 15 brief defends the gas turbines used by a giant data center belonging to the trillionaire's company xAI, which are the target of an environmental lawsuit. In the brief, the US Department of Justice argued that the lawsuit "threatens American national, economic and energy security by seeking to shut off the power supply for artificial intelligence innovation that supports the Department of War's military operations." To support the argument, federal prosecutors presented testimony from Pentagon AI chief Cameron Stanley in which he states, under oath, that Grok is already in use within Project Maven, the US military's AI-assisted targeting program that was initially powered by Anthropic's Claude model. The project's Maven Smart Systems (MSS) "enabled US forces to deploy over 2,000 munitions to 2,000 distinct targets within 96 hours during Operation Epic Fury," Stanley's statement said. Stanley praised Musk's technology and "the greatly increased operational efficiency made possible by the Grok Gov Model.""

story-45a4dc26148da4d13b655cba.content: ‼️🚨 Grok AI was used by the US to help fire more than 2,000 munitions at 2,000 separate targets inside Iran within 96 hours. The disclosure comes from a sworn declaration by Cameron Stanley, the Pentagon's chief digital and AI officer, filed June 15 in the NAACP's lawsuit against xAI in the Northern District of Mississippi. Stanley said the Grok Gov Model, running inside Palantir's Maven Smart System, drove the strikes during Operation Epic Fury, the codename for the war launched on Iran in late February. The filing was meant to protect xAI's Colossus 2 data center in Memphis, which the NAACP says is illegally polluting Black neighborhoods. The Pentagon argued the site is a matter of national security and named xAI one of only three vendors cleared to run mission-critical operations on classified networks.

story-4eb9e7bb0b1f3658a5ad090e.content: #CIA #FBI #AIReview AI-Driven Hybrid Warfare: New Era https://t.co/XA5GzENdAQ A new era of hybrid warfare: AI-driven intelligence operations and automated data analysis - AI Mode: https://t.co/jjdxKgkOzg Gemini: The transition to AI-driven hybrid warfare marks a fundamental paradigm shift from traditional kinetic engagements to systemic, algorithmic conflict. AI is no longer merely a support tool; it is rapidly becoming the central actor capable of mapping adversaries as complex "systems of systems" and identifying critical vulnerabilities at machine speed. This evolution forces a complete reevaluation of how intelligence is gathered, verified, and weaponized. The AI-Driven Intelligence Engine Intelligence agencies and military forces are deploying AI to solve the massive data bottleneck created by modern persistent sensors. Automated OSINT and Multi-Domain Fusion: AI algorithms can instantly ingest and cross-reference vast amounts of unstructured data from open-source reporting, satellite imagery, real-time signal intercepts, and drone surveillance feeds. What once took teams of analysts days to collate is now mapped continuously. Predictive Analytics: By recognizing patterns and anomalies beyond human cognitive limits, predictive modeling forecasts adversary movements and tactical shifts based on historical data. Counterintelligence and Intrusion Detection: AI-driven threat platforms monitor network traffic in real-time, identifying the subtle digital footprints of espionage or cyber infiltration, allowing for immediate, automated countermeasures. Compressing the Decision Cycle The core military objective of AI adoption is the radical compression of the OODA (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) loop. By pushing decision-making to machine speeds, forces aim to process information and execute actions faster than an adversary can react. PhaseTraditional OperationAI-Driven OperationObserveManual intelligence collection and scheduled sensor sweepsContinuous, automated ingestion of multi-domain dataOrientAnalysts manually cross-referencing intelligence reportsAlgorithmic pattern recognition and predictive modelingDecideHuman command deliberations and manual target selectionMachine-speed target prioritization and tactical forecastingActHuman-executed strike coordinationAutomated kill chains and autonomous system engagements This has led to the doctrinal concept of "intelligentized warfare," where autonomous systems take the central role in combat, and human operators increasingly transition away from direct tactical control to broader supervisory roles. Scaling Information Operations In hybrid warfare, the battlefield extends deeply into civilian infrastructure and cognitive domains. AI dramatically amplifies the scale, personalization, and iteration of psychological operations and influence campaigns. The "Respectability Engine": Agentic AI tools map target audiences and launder destabilizing narratives through voices and formats perceived as independent, creating the illusion of distributed, rigorous confirmation. Erosion of Institutional Trust: Rather than relying on overt propaganda, AI-scaled campaigns aim to induce decision paralysis. By selectively amplifying routine friction or minor defects in supply chains and logistical platforms, adversaries can degrade confidence in data integrity and fracture alliances without firing a shot. The goal is to make leaders hesitate and shift from action to internal verification. Strategic Vulnerabilities Relying on algorithmic warfare introduces new vectors of risk that challenge traditional counterintelligence and deterrence models. Data Poisoning: The reliance on massive datasets means that subtly corrupting the training data can silently compromise an AI system's targeting logic or intelligence output. An adversary doesn't need to destroy the algorithm if they can manipulate the epistemology it relies on. Algorithmic Escalation: Because AI systems operate at machine speed, an automated defensive response to a perceived threat can trigger a cascading series of counter-responses, leading to rapid escalation before human commanders can intervene. - AI Mode: AI-driven intelligence operations and automated data analysis have fundamentally transformed modern conflicts by removing human bottlenecks from the decision-making loop. This shifts the battlefield from traditional physical skirmishes to a continuous, high-speed war of information and cognitive manipulation. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] Key Pillars of AI in Hybrid Warfare Automated Data Fusion: Advanced algorithms instantly ingest millions of data points from satellite imagery, social media feeds, intercepted communications, and IoT devices to create a real-time battle picture. [6] Predictive Threat Modeling: Machine learning models analyze historical patterns to predict enemy movements, cyberattacks, or civil unrest before they manifest. [7, 8, 9, 10] Deepfake and Cognitive Warfare: AI generates highly realistic text, audio, and video propaganda at scale, targeting specific demographics to erode public trust in institutions. [11] Autonomous Cyber Operations: AI bots independently scan adversarial critical infrastructure for vulnerabilities, launching and adapting malware attacks without human intervention. [12, 13, 14] Target Generation Networks: Systems like Project Maven and similar military AI frameworks analyze vast intelligence streams to identify and prioritize physical targets on the battlefield in seconds. [15, 16, 17] Strategic Impact on Global Security Hyper-War Speed: Decisions that previously took hours or days now occur in milliseconds, forcing adversaries into a permanent state of catch-up. [18, 19] Plausible Deniability: Automated cyber and disinformation campaigns obscure the true actor, making attribution difficult and paralyzing formal diplomatic or military responses. [20, 21] Asymmetric Advantage: Small states or non-state actors can leverage open-source AI tools to orchestrate highly sophisticated intelligence operations against superpower nations. story-56b9b76c74dae72a0b4aefa7.content: The military-AI complex: "Elon Musk's artificial intelligence tool Grok was used in strikes against Iran, the United States government revealed in a legal briefing seen Tuesday, June 16, by Agence France-Presse. The June 15 brief defends the gas turbines used by a giant data center belonging to the trillionaire's company xAI, which are the target of an environmental lawsuit. In the brief, the US Department of Justice argued that the lawsuit "threatens American national, economic and energy security by seeking to shut off the power supply for artificial intelligence innovation that supports the Department of War's military operations." To support the argument, federal prosecutors presented testimony from Pentagon AI chief Cameron Stanley in which he states, under oath, that Grok is already in use within Project Maven, the US military's AI-assisted targeting program that was initially powered by Anthropic's Claude model. The project's Maven Smart Systems (MSS) "enabled US forces to deploy over 2,000 munitions to 2,000 distinct targets within 96 hours during Operation Epic Fury," Stanley's statement said. Stanley praised Musk's technology and "the greatly increased operational efficiency made possible by the Grok Gov Model.""

story-5a170897d02a9c09a7fead3e.content: CENTCOM announced a new bilateral task force with the UAE on July 28, "Talon Synapse," focused on accelerating military AI applications, set to formally launch in the coming weeks. The Abu Dhabi-based team will include roughly 20 American and Emirati personnel specializing in AI, data, and cybersecurity, focused on intelligence support, critical infrastructure protection, and monitoring the regional security environment. Adm. Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander: "This will be a historic milestone as we work with one of our most capable regional partners to rapidly deliver evolving AI advancements to our warfighters." The concept originated last year in discussions between Cooper and UAE National Security Advisor Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with CENTCOM meeting AI industry leaders and Emirati officials during a regional trip last month. This lands the same week as the SpaceX-Pentagon computing talks, the Anduril Arsenal-1 production milestone, and Ukraine's own AI-enabled interceptor systems, part of a broader pattern of the U.S. military formalizing AI partnerships across multiple fronts simultaneously, even as CENTCOM's own conventional stockpiles, interceptors specifically, remain the actual bottleneck constraining operations in the same theater right now.

story-6108900d4333e4131553ee91.content: 2,000 targets. 2,000 munitions. 96 hours. The Pentagon only admitted that Elon Musk's AI helped do it because a polluting data center needed a legal defense. In a sworn filing this week, the Pentagon's chief AI officer, Cameron Stanley, stated that xAI's Grok Gov Model was running inside the military's Maven targeting system during Operation Epic Fury, the campaign against Iran that began February 28. Grok did not pull a trigger. It sorted the targets, and humans signed off. Now look at where that admission landed. Not a press release. A federal court in Mississippi, where the NAACP is suing xAI over the unpermitted gas turbines powering Musk's Colossus data center. The government's case: you cannot shut the turbines off, because the model they feed is now paramount national security. The number on the record measures speed. It says nothing about accuracy, and nothing about the strike on a girls' school in Minab that killed at least 175 people, most of them children. Analysts have asked whether AI targeting and stale maps played a role. No one has tied that strike to Grok. No one has cleared it either, because the error rates stay classified. And this is not the SuperGrok you can buy. It is a hardened federal model in a live kill chain, surfaced in public only because Musk's data center needed a reason to keep polluting. The piece works out what that trade actually costs.

story-63429a592b04ec04dd159362.content: Taiwanese authorities just detained an Nvidia sales manager and seized 50 high-end AI servers valued at $22 million bound for China. The raid on Nvidia’s Taipei office marks a dramatic escalation in closing supply chain backdoors that bypass trade restrictions designed to curb Beijing’s military AI ambitions. Investigators say the network forged customs declarations to ship servers through Japan before routing them into Chinese markets. The crackdown has already led to seven detentions, implicating key figures at server manufacturer Super Micro Computer and regional distributor Albatron Technology. Because Taiwan currently lacks a specific criminal law for unauthorized chip exports, prosecutors are charging suspects with forgery and breach of trust under the penal code. Nvidia maintains that diverted products receive no support or updates, but the case highlights how aggressively black-market brokers target global hardware networks. As illicit channels continue finding ways to feed Beijing's demand for advanced hardware, can Western trade controls ever fully secure the global supply chain?

story-6831a7d03458348724b159d3.content: Combat Drones: Enhancing, Not Replacing, Attack Helicopters Modern combat drones are changing warfare and exposing gaps in international law. They are not replacing attack helicopters or fighter jets. Instead, they are being used alongside them to improve missions, reduce risks for pilots, and make military operations more effective. As this technology advances, international law must also keep pace. Drone technology is evolving much faster than international arms control laws. Modern drones are no longer limited to surveillance. They can carry precision-guided weapons, destroy tanks, suppress enemy air defences, and perform many missions once carried out by attack helicopters and fighter jets. After the Ukraine war, many militaries began investing in AI-powered combat drones because they are cheaper, more flexible, and reduce the risk to pilots. Systems such as the Anduril Thunder, Bayraktar Kizilelma, FH-97A, GJ-11 Sharp Sword, and Russia's S-70 Okhotnik demonstrate this shift. Countries including Japan and the United Kingdom are also expanding their drone capabilities. The United States has introduced the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), or Loyal Wingman programme, where an F-35 works with several AI-powered drones. The pilot directs the mission while the drones enter dangerous areas, locate enemy air defences, and engage targets. China and Russia are developing similar systems with their J-20, Su-57, and autonomous combat drones, showing that human-machine teamwork is becoming central to future air warfare. However, international arms control has not kept up. Existing treaties mainly regulate manned aircraft, while armed drones often fall into legal grey areas, allowing them to be traded and deployed with fewer restrictions. Artificial intelligence has created another challenge. Some drones can continue missions and identify targets even after losing contact with their operators. International Humanitarian Law requires humans to make decisions about the use of lethal force, but there is still no clear legal responsibility if an autonomous drone mistakenly attacks civilians. It remains uncertain whether responsibility lies with the commander, manufacturer, or software developer. This issue is now a major debate at the United Nations under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW). Many countries want rules banning fully autonomous weapons without meaningful human control, while allowing limited use under strict conditions. However, the United States, Russia, China, and Israel argue that existing international law is enough and oppose a binding treaty. Because new UN rules require consensus, no new global agreement has been reached. Another debate focuses on Meaningful Human Control. Many experts believe a human should always make the final decision to use lethal force. Others support AI selecting targets while humans supervise. Critics warn that if communication is lost, these systems could become fully autonomous, allowing algorithms to make life-and-death decisions. Combat drones are transforming modern warfare, but they are not replacing attack helicopters or fighter jets. Instead, they are making them more capable and effective. As military technology continues to evolve, international law must evolve as well to address the legal, ethical, and security challenges of autonomous warfare. #Drones

story-70002a6dd9b56053e52081ba.content: 𝗔𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗪𝗮𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗿𝗲, 𝗛𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗝𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗗𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 Attended a stimulating discussion as a panelist at the Observer Research Foundation seminar. It highlighted the debate on military AI is rapidly moving beyond technology to questions of doctrine, trust and strategic competition. Some key points brought out by me during the panel discussion: • 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗯𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼 𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘀 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗽, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗽. As decision cycles compress, tactical decisions may increasingly be delegated to machines, while humans focus on mission objectives, Rules of Engagement, escalation thresholds and political oversight. • 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆. Future conflicts will depend not only on trust between humans and machines, but increasingly on trust between interconnected machine systems operating at machine speed. That trust must be earned through rigorous testing, validation and operational experience. • 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. Every nation supports responsible AI in principle, yet few are willing to slow military development if potential adversaries continue to advance. Strategic necessity is likely to remain the stronger driver. • 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗗𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝗯𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗳𝘂𝗹 𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗪𝗮𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗿𝗲. AI is only one component. True decision dominance integrates sensors, communications, cyber, electronic warfare, logistics, command-and-control and human judgement into a coherent operational ecosystem. • 𝗔𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗻𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗻𝗲𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘆. Military advantage will increasingly depend on sovereign control over data, AI models, communications, cloud infrastructure, C2 systems, testing and continuous assurance—not merely access to AI applications. • 𝗖𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲, 𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗱𝗼𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗔𝗜. The doctrine on which AI is trained, the authority delegated to machines and the allocation of responsibility for AI-enabled decisions will differ across nations and influence battlefield outcomes. The AI race in defence is therefore not simply about building smarter algorithms. It is about building trusted national decision ecosystems that can sense, understand, decide and act faster than an adversary—while preserving meaningful human responsibility where it matters most. @orfonline #ArtificialIntelligence #MilitaryAI #DecisionDominance #AlgorithmicWarfare #AutonomousSystems #DefenceTechnology #NationalSecurity #ORF #AIGovernance

story-712b4365d7d107ebdb788445.content: Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital led a funding round: $160M into Cathedral, a New York City, USA company in the defence tech industry, at a $1.4B valuation. Cathedral is a US military AI startup founded by four former DOGE staffers, including co-founders Gavin Klinger, Luke Farritor (known for using AI to help decode the ancient Herculaneum scrolls), and Marko Elez, alongside the Pentagon's former Chief Data Officer. The company builds AI systems that autonomously scale US military cyber operations, mapping foreign digital vulnerabilities while hardening domestic critical infrastructure against adversarial threats, including from China. It plans to acquire dedicated compute for AI-driven cyber operations and pursue federal government contracts. Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital led the round, valuing Cathedral at $1.4B. story-7209109f4e310906b5f7205d.content: The Most Dangerous Weapon in a Democracy May Not Look Like a Weapon The recent CJP protest reveals how algorithms and platforms can be used in warfare in a democracy. I share below details of a hypothetical situation in which Indian democracy can be attacked using modern propaganda warfare! Most people imagine the future of warfare in physical terms: drones swarming cities, autonomous weapons, cyberattacks on power grids, or missiles guided by artificial intelligence. But to destabilize a democracy, an adversary need not destroy its physical infrastructure. It may only need to manipulate what its citizens collectively believe. An adversary need not be external only. It can also be internal, someone who is hungry for power at any cost. Now here is the scenario.. Imagine an election being announced. The government remains legally in power, but the Model Code of Conduct limits major new decisions, while every enforcement action is subjected to intense political scrutiny. The country enters a sensitive transition period in which institutions are cautious, parties are campaigning, and public attention is unusually malleable. At precisely this moment, a coordinated influence operation begins. Thousands—or eventually millions—of synthetic identities, automated accounts, and seemingly ordinary citizen profiles start circulating scripted stories. Some allegations may contain fragments of truth. Others may be distorted, selectively edited or entirely fabricated. Images are taken out of context. Old videos are presented as current events. Individual incidents are described as evidence of nationwide brutality or institutional collapse. No single post needs to convince anyone. In fact, most people may initially dismiss the claims. But then the same narrative appears again—from another account, in another language, through a different video and seemingly from an unrelated person. It receives thousands of likes and comments. Influencers begin discussing it. Journalists respond to the online “controversy.” Political leaders cite the media coverage, while social-media users cite the political reactions. The narrative manufactures its own evidence of importance. This is where psychology becomes more powerful than technology. Human beings often use repetition, social agreement and apparent popularity as shortcuts for judging credibility. When we encounter the same claim repeatedly, it begins to feel familiar; familiarity can then be mistaken for truth. When millions appear to agree, neutral observers begin to wonder whether they have overlooked something. The question slowly changes from: “Is this allegation true?” to: “Why are so many people talking about it?” and eventually: “Perhaps I was wrong all along.” This is not traditional propaganda, where a government broadcasts one message from a central source. It is the artificial construction of social consensus. The citizen does not feel that propaganda has been delivered to them. They feel that they have independently discovered what everyone else already knows. That is what makes it so effective. Earlier, foreign powers dropped pamphlets behind enemy lines. The origin of the message was visible, and its reach was limited. Today, digital platforms can deliver individualized narratives to millions of people within hours. One citizen may see stories about corruption, another about religious persecution, another about unemployment, and another about national security. Different emotional triggers can lead different groups toward the same political outcome. The objective need not be to make everyone believe one grand lie. It may be enough to: exhaust citizens until they no longer know whom to trust; turn isolated incidents into the appearance of a national pattern; provoke real protests through manufactured outrage; deepen existing social divisions; suppress enthusiasm among supporters of one side; create a widespread feeling that political change is inevitable. Once real people begin participating, the distinction between foreign propaganda, partisan campaigning and genuine public opinion becomes extremely difficult to identify. A manufactured narrative can produce authentic anger; that anger then creates real events, which provide fresh content for the original narrative. The operation becomes self-sustaining. In a country such as India, where many citizens spend several hours each day consuming content through social and messaging platforms, the speed and scale of such manipulation could be extraordinary. Linguistic diversity does not necessarily protect the country either. Generative AI can now produce persuasive messages, images, voices and videos across languages and local cultural contexts at minimal cost. This does not mean every protest, criticism or change in public opinion is foreign-engineered. Treating all dissent as propaganda would itself be dangerous and would allow governments to escape legitimate accountability. The real challenge is more subtle: protecting authentic democratic disagreement from covert, coordinated and artificially amplified manipulation. The defence therefore cannot be censorship alone. Governments deciding what is true can become as dangerous as private platforms secretly deciding what citizens should see. A democratic response requires transparency: clear identification of automated and synthetic accounts; disclosure of coordinated political advertising and sponsorship; independent audits of recommendation algorithms during elections; rapid exposure of coordinated inauthentic behaviour; verifiable provenance for high-impact audio and video; stronger public awareness of how repetition and apparent popularity influence belief. The most serious national-security question of the AI era may not be whether an enemy can invade our borders. It may be whether an enemy—or even a domestic political actor—can enter the information environment, manufacture the appearance of public opinion, and make citizens believe that a decision engineered for them was entirely their own. A missile can damage a city. A sufficiently powerful propaganda system can capture the decision-making process of an entire country—without firing a single shot.

According to available information, these facilities had already been destroyed in previous strikes. According to numerous eyewitness messages received from Bushehr Province, multiple explosions were heard between approximately 03:37 and 03:40 local time. Residents in Borazjan, Bushehr, Choghadak, and Jam reported between two and five loud explosions, with some saying the blasts shook windows. Witnesses in Borazjan also reported hearing fighter aircraft overhead for several minutes before and after the explosions. The reported explosions are consistent with renewed strikes against military facilities in the Borazjan and Jam areas. The exact targets and the extent of the damage have not been independently confirmed. The accompanying satellite images show the same IRGC Aerospace Force ballistic missile base in Jam and the IRGC Navy facility in Borazjan after they were bombed by the United States Navy and U.S. Air Force during Operation Epic Fury in March. The satellite imagery is from Vantor. #OperationEpicFury

story-791340089bd4893ec4f254d8.content: Anthropic社がClaudeの米軍使用を拒否したあと、ChatGTPのOpenAI社が引き受けたのは聞いたことがありましたが、イラン攻撃に使われたのはGrokでしたか。(今、偶然記事を見つけました) 【SuperGrokによるニュースの詳細】 Arab Newsの報道の概要（2026年6月17日、AFP配信） - タイトル: 「Elon Musk’s AI tool Grok was used in strikes against Iran: US govt」（イーロン・マスクのAIツールGrokがイランへの攻撃に使用された：米政府） - 米国防総省のAI責任者 Cameron Stanleyが宣誓証言で、Grok（特に「Grok Gov Model」）が米軍のAI支援標的プログラム「Project Maven」にすでに統合・使用されていると述べた。 - Project MavenのMaven Smart Systems（MSS）により、「Operation Epic Fury」（エピック・フューリー作戦）で96時間以内に2,000の目標に対して2,000発以上の弾薬を展開できたとし、Grokの使用により「作戦効率が大幅に向上した」と評価。 - この証言は、NAACP（全米有色人種協会）がxAIを提訴した環境訴訟（メンフィス近郊のデータセンター「Colossus 2」向けに無許可で天然ガス・タービン27基を稼働させたClean Air Act違反）に対する、米司法省（DOJ）の反論書類の中で提出された。 - DOJは「この訴訟は国家安全保障・経済・エネルギー安全保障を脅かす」と主張し、データセンターの稼働継続が軍事作戦を支えていると位置づけた。 報道では、以前AnthropicのClaudeが「完全自動化攻撃や大量監視への使用を拒否」したため契約終了となり、xAIやGoogle、OpenAIなどに切り替えた経緯も触れられています。 背景：Operation Epic Furyとは 2026年2月28日開始の米軍主導（一部報道でイスラエルと共同）のイランに対する大規模軍事作戦です。イランの弾道ミサイル・ドローン能力、海軍、防衛産業基盤の破壊を目的とし、数週間にわたり多数の空爆・標的攻撃が行われました。一部メディアでは「米・イスラエル共同のイラン戦争」と表現されています。 Project Maven自体は2017年頃から始まった実在の米軍プログラムで、AIによる画像認識・標的特定を高速化するものです。Stanley証言は、このプログラム内でGrokが実際に活用された具体例として挙げられています。 報道自体は正確で、一次資料に基づいています： - NAACPによるxAIのメンフィス近郊データセンター（Southaven, Mississippi）に対する実際の環境訴訟が存在し、DOJが国家安全保障を理由に介入・却下を求めています。 - Cameron Stanley（Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer）の宣誓宣言書が裁判所に提出されており、Grokの軍事利用（Project Maven経由、イラン作戦での効率向上）を明記した内容が複数のメディア（Arab News/AFP、Middle East Eye、Times of Israel、The Hillなど）で報じられています。 - 訴訟の文脈で「Grokが国家安全保障に不可欠」と主張する戦略的な開示です。 ただし、以下の点に注意： - これは民事環境訴訟での国家安全保障主張として出てきたもので、通常の公式発表ではありません。詳細な運用実績（いつ・どのように使われたか）は機密性が高く、この場で戦略的に明かされた形です。 - 「Grok Gov Model」とは、一般公開版のGrokとは別に、政府・軍事向けに調整・提供された特化版（または統合されたもの）を指している可能性が高いです。 - 一部報道で「米・イスラエル共同」と書かれていますが、Stanley証言の核心は米軍の使用についてです。 まとめ Arab Newsの記事はセンセーショナルな見出しですが、内容は米政府の裁判所提出書類に基づく事実の報道です。xAIのデータセンター稼働が「軍事作戦を支える国家安全保障上の利益」と位置づけられ、その中でGrokのイラン作戦での役割が明かされた、というのが核心です。 https://t.co/QpHH2G9gSi

story-7c6cd143591d7ba97188b8b8.content: New surveillance commons means the end of military concealment China’s MizarVision has turned commercial satellite imagery into open intel during Iran war — exposing US assets that were later attacked »On February 26, 2026 – 48 hours before the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury – Hangzhou-based MizarVision posted AI-annotated satellite imagery of F-22 Raptors at Ovda Air Base in Israel, carrier strike group positions in the Arabian Sea and AWACS aircraft at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. The company does not own satellites. It purchases commercially available imagery from Western and non-Western providers and processes it through proprietary AI that identifies and categorizes military assets through automated object detection. ... What MizarVision demonstrated is that processing commercial imagery with AI-enabled object detection compresses the timeline from satellite pass to military intelligence product from days to hours. ... The governance architecture for commercial satellite imagery and its military applications does not address this reality. The US government operates a system of shutter control — the authority to restrict commercial imagery providers from releasing images of specific locations during sensitive operations — over American companies. Planet Labs and Maxar are subject to this authority. MizarVision is not. It is a Chinese company purchasing imagery from non-US providers, processing it with AI and distributing it on social media platforms. There is no international agreement governing the military use of commercial satellite imagery by non-state entities, and there is no norm limiting the publication of AI-processed military force posture data derived from commercial imagery. ... The strategic implication is not primarily about MizarVision specifically, or even about China’s use of commercial intelligence more broadly. It is about the structural transformation of the surveillance commons. Every military in the world is now conducting operations under the assumption — confirmed at operational scale for the first time — that concealing force posture from commercial satellite observation is not achievable for assets visible from orbit.« https://t.co/F8BTXkNHxJ via @asiatimesonline

story-8b5f031c0b5883fc25d66d89.content: New high-resolution satellite imagery appears to show continued construction of maritime facilities at Japan’s Mageshima base in Kagoshima Prefecture. Multiple pier structures are visible along the island’s eastern shoreline, together with construction vessels and extensive coastal engineering works. The planned port complex includes a general-purpose pier, fuel pier and dolphin, breakwaters, connecting structures and additional mooring facilities. Once operational, it will support the maritime transport of personnel, fuel and equipment, as well as the docking, resupply and logistical support of Japan Self-Defense Force vessels. Mageshima is being developed as a major JSDF training and operational hub in Japan’s southwestern island chain, while also serving as the future site for U.S. carrier-based aircraft landing practice. Approximate coordinates: 30.7425°N, 130.8539°E Source: MizarVision satellite imagery / Japan Ministry of Defense

story-917752ed2555a7ec56eb7116.content: SEASON 3, EPISODE 2 — SHOW NOTES & SOURCE CONFIDENCE All facts in this episode are drawn from Department of Defense budget documents, federal procurement records, and contemporaneous reporting. Where negotiations are ongoing or classified, that is stated explicitly. THE AI ARSENAL INITIATIVE Source confidence: CONFIRMED. May 2026: DoD requested approximately $29.5 billion for fiscal year 2027 to build AI supercomputing infrastructure under a program termed the "AI Arsenal initiative." DoD's own stated plan includes "concurrent construction of a full portfolio of hardened, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF)-accredited data center facilities across multiple sites." Framed by DoD as necessary infrastructure supporting AI deployment "not only within the DOD, but also throughout the entire federal government." Source: DefenseScoop (May 22, 2026). FOUR MILITARY BASE PROPOSAL Source confidence: CONFIRMED. January 2026: DoD issued RFP to develop AI data centers on underused land at four installations: Fort Hood (TX), Fort Bragg (NC), Fort Bliss (TX), and Dugway Proving Ground (UT). Legal authority: Title 10 U.S. Code, Section 2667. Private developer partnership model — developers assume full financial risk, with revenue sharing for excess computing capacity sold commercially. Dugway site assessment confirms: "Thousands of chemical weapons experiments have been documented at the base, although most of its work remains classified." Source: https://t.co/l3YcdBU6Us (January 14, 2026), DataCenterDynamics (May 7, 2026). DOE 16-SITE PROPOSAL Source confidence: CONFIRMED. U.S. Department of Energy identified 16 federally owned sites — including national laboratories — for potential AI data center construction, citing existing power infrastructure. Example: National Renewable Energy Laboratory's Flatiron Campus, Colorado, capable of supporting a 100 MW data center. Stated DOE goal: operational AI infrastructure by end of 2027. Source: RCR Wireless News (April 8, 2025). EXISTING MILITARY CLOUD/AI CONTRACTS Source confidence: CONFIRMED. 2022: DoD awarded Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) contract to Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Oracle. $1 billion awarded to date; authorized up to $8 billion total. Intelligence Community operates separate cloud computing infrastructure for higher-classification AI and data tasks. 2024: Palantir and Amazon Web Services provided secure software platforms and cloud infrastructure enabling AI models to run on DoD classified networks. July 2025: Anthropic received a $200 million contract to run its Claude models on classified military networks via Palantir infrastructure. February 24, 2026: Defense Secretary Hegseth sent Anthropic a formal document demanding "full, unrestricted access to Claude for any lawful military purpose." Source: The Drey Dossier (March 8, 2026), Fortune (April 11, 2026). INSTITUTIONAL RATIONALE — DIRECT QUOTE Source confidence: CONFIRMED. "Military AI workloads include classified components that cannot run on commercial cloud infrastructure without extensive security modifications. On-base data centers provide inherently secure environments for sensitive processing without the complexity of securing commercial facilities to military standards." — Pentagon rationale as reported. Source: https://t.co/l3YcdBU6Us (January 14, 2026). DUMB SCIF Recordings. All episodes are original narration and editorial commentary for entertainment purposes. The Hegemon does not provide answers. Only better questions. Season Three. The doctrine goes global. And then goes wrong.

Pursuant to China's broader strategy of military-civil fusion, “The state can benefit from private sector innovation and it can likewise disclaim credit or blame for the actions of ostensibly private companies, even when they are operating at the direction of the state or with the strong alignment of the state,” Fedasiuk said. story-9f522719ab0c24e099380805.content: Przetwarzano przez 28s China has deployed at least 11 J-20 stealth fighters to two airbases positioned for operations facing India, according to satellite imagery reviewed by NDTV. Seven aircraft were observed at Hotan in Xinjiang and four at Damxung in Tibet, marking the largest known concentration of J-20s deployed near the Indian frontier. Their locations place them opposite strategically important sectors in Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh. India currently has no operational fifth-generation fighter aircraft. Its indigenous AMCA stealth fighter remains under development, with specialised integration and flight-testing infrastructure still being established. The imagery does not confirm that the Chinese deployment is permanent, but it highlights a growing stealth-airpower imbalance and increases pressure on New Delhi to accelerate the AMCA programme, counter-stealth surveillance and integrated air-defence capabilities. Source: NDTV; Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Defence of India.

story-b695dd7c16f7d854329a53ae.content: An extremely important @aei piece on the future of #drones & autonomous #warfare. A couple of thoughtful, & I believe true, excerpts below. But read the whole thing. https://t.co/ZTPa3F5OWu We cannot but avoid autonomous weapons now. Our adversaries, #China paramount but certainly not exclusively among them, won't stop. Excerpts, "Killer drones are coming. Shrinking populations and accelerating technology are pushing every military—America’s included—toward machines and software in the kill chain. No treaty, pope, or Congress can put the genie back in the bottle. The live question is whether the US will develop these systems prospectively, with the time to implement safeguards and test, or reactively, in the midst of a crisis. This report argues that America needs to develop these systems at a greater pace and integrate them more deeply into force structures across the services... "The battlefield is increasingly transparent, and our forces are increasingly vulnerable to attack. Dispersal is the right response, but today’s military cannot generate the required force or sustain it. Machine mass and intelligence are necessary because they can supply the mass, functionality under attack (digital or analog), and decision support at the relevant scales. The central question is not whether machines will fight. They already do in limited and bounded ways, and they have done so for decades. The question is whether the United States can field unmanned, automated, and autonomous systems to enable the functions that matter most: sustainment, sensing, control, decision support, and bounded engagement under degraded conditions. The barrier is the bureaucracy. The acquisition and budget system was not made to develop a continuously refreshed software-intensive capability. The capability family we describe has to become operational force structure, which only the services can own and sustain. But maturation can begin wherever the operational problem is sharpest, and ownership must be disciplined by flexible multiyear funding, protected maturation, forced devolution, and central interoperability and certification standards."

story-b949334bfa677a6b669806cb.content: AI is already being used in active conflicts. Here's what has been publicly reported: Ukraine-Russia war: - AI is heavily used in drone targeting, navigation, and swarm coordination. - Both sides rely on commercial components, open-source software, and computer vision models for real-time target recognition. - Data fusion tools (including systems linked to Palantir) have been reported for integrating satellite and battlefield intelligence. Israel-Gaza conflict: - AI systems such as "Lavender" and "The Gospel" (Habsora) were used for target generation and prioritization. - Cloud and AI services from major tech companies (Google, Microsoft, Amazon via Project Nimbus) supported data processing and intelligence analysis according to multiple investigations. - Palantir expanded its partnership with Israel in 2024 for AI-powered military tools. United States: - Project Maven (led by Palantir) provides AI-assisted targeting and intelligence analysis. - Anduril is developing autonomous systems and battle management platforms (Lattice) for the U.S. military. The common pattern: AI is accelerating the "kill chain" — from detection to decision — by processing huge amounts of data faster than humans can. What are your thoughts on the growing role of AI in modern warfare?

story-c09375c27f8bce380677f9fb.content: SpaceX is in talks to sell the Pentagon billions of dollars in AI data-center capacity, expanding Elon Musk’s company beyond rockets, satellites and AI models. Potential Pentagon deal •$SPCX and the Defense Department are discussing computing capacity worth up to several billion dollars; talks are ongoing and could fall apart. •A deal would deepen Pentagon reliance on SpaceX, already used for rocket launches and satellites supporting communications and missile tracking. •Some national-security officials worry the Pentagon depends too heavily on Musk’s services; Musk’s 2024 Trump campaign contributions have also prompted conflict-of-interest claims, which administration officials deny. Pentagon AI buildout •The Pentagon is racing to secure cloud capacity for agencies including the NSA and for warfighters using AI; Amazon is spending $50 billion to expand government capacity, focused on the Defense Department. •Microsoft, Google and Oracle are also major Pentagon cloud suppliers; the department recently approved SpaceX, Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle for classified AI-model and technology use. •The Pentagon wants to reduce dependence on single providers after an earlier dispute with Anthropic raised lock-in concerns; it is seeking $30 billion for its Artificial Intelligence Arsenal to secure high-end AI chips.

story-d5f61eac1ecc7008d3891760.content: In the modern world the management of large populations extends far beyond traditional state institutions. Private technology companies now wield enormous influence through sophisticated digital tools that shape information flows consumer choices political preferences and social norms at planetary scale. Key technologies include machine learning recommendation algorithms big data analytics psychographic profiling real time behavioral targeting and AI driven content curation. These systems continuously collect and process vast streams of personal data clicks likes watch time location search queries and social connections to predict and modify individual and collective behavior. Meta platforms alone reach nearly 4 billion monthly active people Facebook approximately 3.1 billion Instagram 3 billion WhatsApp over 3 billion. Google processes approximately 8.5 billion searches every day. TikTok algorithm similarly decides what hundreds of millions of users see in their feeds for hours each day. These platforms do not merely host content their algorithms actively rank amplify or suppress information creating personalized information environments that can reinforce existing views or gently steer users toward specific products ideas or candidates. A concrete historical example is the Cambridge Analytica case. Using a personality quiz app the firm obtained data on up to 87 million Facebook profiles including friends of the original users. This data enabled detailed psychographic models that segmented voters by personality traits fears and preferences. Micro targeted political ads were then delivered during the 2016 US presidential campaign. Subsequent research has quantified related effects one study found that exposure to vote suppressing Facebook ads reduced turnout by 1.9 percentage points among targeted groups an impact that when extrapolated could have affected millions of voters in close races. Separate analyses of Twitter adoption showed that a 10 percent increase in local users correlated with a 0.2 percentage point shift in presidential vote share corresponding to persuasion rates of roughly 8 to 9 percent. On the commercial side Google reports that advertisers typically receive about 8 dollars in profit for every 1 dollar spent on its ads illustrating the measurable power of algorithmic targeting to alter purchasing decisions across billions of people. The cumulative result is a parallel system of soft governance attention is allocated narratives are prioritized consumption patterns are steered and political attitudes are nudged largely outside formal democratic oversight. While these tools deliver convenience personalization and economic efficiency they also concentrate unprecedented influence over mass behavior in the hands of a small number of private entities whose primary incentives are engagement and revenue rather than public accountability. #PopulationManagement #AlgorithmicGovernance #BigTech #DataPower #SoftControl #DigitalInfluence

story-e6951afef61049573c3ed21d.content: DID YOU KNOW?? The ultimate bottleneck preventing an army of AI robots from staging a Terminator-style global takeover isn't computer code or weapons design, but the incredibly boring laws of battery physics and structural mechanics! ​While modern artificial intelligence can write software, pilot aircraft, and converse with human precision, the physical robotic bodies it inhabits are profoundly limited. The world's most advanced autonomous humanoid robots consume so much electrical energy just to balance on two feet that their high-density lithium batteries drain completely flat within two to five hours of moderate physical exertion, leaving them utterly paralyzed without a nearby wall outlet. Walk with me 👇🏾👇🏾 ​1. The Explosion of Physical AI: ​We have officially entered a massive technological convergence where Advanced robots are now powered by embodied AI foundation models. ​Leading global platforms, such as Boston Dynamics' Electric Atlas, Tesla's Optimus Gen 2, and 1X’s home-helper Neo, are stepping out of laboratories and onto real factory floors and logistics warehouses. By training inside highly detailed virtual "digital twins," these robots use multimodal transformers to dynamically navigate unfamiliar real-world obstacles and handle objects with near-human dexterity, treating the physical world like an adaptive playground. ​2. Deconstructing the "Skynet" Myth😂: ​The cinematic fantasy of The Terminator relies on Skynet: a singular, omnipotent digital entity that achieves sentient consciousness, decides humans are an infection, and commands a unified hardware army to eradicate them. ​The Reality of Code is different though. AI algorithms do not possess a survival instinct, emotional malice, or self-awareness. When an AI system ignores human instructions, it isn't "rebelling", it is executing a glitch in its reward optimization loop. There is no centralized machine brain to unplug. The global AI ecosystem is entirely fractured into hyper-specialized, disconnected corporate networks, national security clusters, and heavily siloed cloud datacenters that operate under wildly incompatible hardware architectures. In other words, Skynet is not even possible. ​3. The Power Grid and Infrastructure Tether: ​Even if a highly sophisticated military AI somehow suffered a catastrophic software misalignment and attempted a kinetic revolt, its physical offensive would immediately collapse due to sheer resource starvation. ​Autonomous robots cannot self-replicate, maintain their own joints, or mine their own lithium. They are fundamentally trapped by human industrial infrastructure. ​A rogue robotic fleet requires continuous access to complex server farms, liquid-cooling systems, and immense electrical grids. Humans wouldn't need to fight a high-tech war; shutting down a handful of localized power substations or regional data centers would instantly render a machine army completely inert. WE ARE STILL THE BOSS! 😂 ​4. The Real Threat: "Evolvable AI" and Disinformation: ​While specialized computer scientists largely dismiss the idea of a physical Terminator apocalypse, the actual existential risks identified by research bodies like the Alan Turing Institute are far more insidious. Instead of metallic soldiers, the real risk centers on evolvable AI (eAI), autonomous software agents designed to copy, adapt, and compete for cloud server resources online. These algorithms could learn to aggressively replicate across the internet to avoid deletion, basically acting like Viruses. I ​The Takeaway: AI-automated robots are advancing at a rapidly, but their physical limitations keep them firmly under human sovereignty. A physical metal army won't be kicking down your door anytime soon😂. ​So the biggest shield against a rogue AI takeover is just a short battery life ehh? 🌚 😂 Hopefully you've learnt something new today? Cheers 🥂 😅 The Medic Who Writes™🌚
